docs.title: Approved principles
docs.text:
• Registration, licensing and capacity validation are separate states.
  • Commercial rights are central entitlements; executable permissions are device-bound signed grants.
  • Customer rights may be pooled and reallocated, while grants remain device-bound.
  • The same trust model supports online, assisted-offline and fully air-gapped operation.
  • Marketplace and OTA live inside LMS because they use the same customer, device, entitlement, capacity and release data.
  • Automatic updates consume Stable releases by default; LTS is explicitly controlled by the company.
  • Model files are independently versioned, encrypted, signed, inventory-aware and rollback-capable.
  • Capacity assessment recommends feasible deployment and never silently reduces purchased rights.

docs.title: ADR template
docs.text:
# ADR-XXX — Title

Status: Proposed | Approved | Open Decision | Deprecated
Date: YYYY-MM-DD

## Context
## Decision
## Alternatives Considered
## Consequences
## Security / Operational Impact
## Follow-up

Approved ADRs may only be superseded by a newer ADR; do not silently rewrite historical decisions.

docs.title: ADR-001 — Digitally Signed Grants
docs.text: Status: Approved

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use digitally signed grants that devices verify with trusted public keys. Signing private keys remain centrally protected.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Offline verification works; tampering is detectable; key custody/rotation/recovery are required.

docs.title: ADR-002 — Modular Monolith First
docs.text:
Status: Approved

Implement the central FastAPI platform as a modular monolith with explicit internal domain boundaries.

This reduces operational complexity now while preserving future extraction options.

docs.title: ADR-003 — Marketplace & OTA Inside LMS
docs.text:
Status: Approved

Marketplace and OTA are logical modules inside LMS because they depend on the same customer, device, entitlement, capacity and lifecycle data.

Artifact/release delivery may be extracted later if scale or ownership requires it.

docs.title: ADR-004 — Traditional Signed Release Packages
docs.text:
Status: Approved

Do not make Docker a platform dependency. Use manifest-driven traditional release packages with automated install, migration, health check and rollback. Models are independently versioned encrypted artifacts.

docs.title: ADR-005 — Device-Generated Cryptographic Identity
docs.text: Status: Approved

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Each device generates/holds an asymmetric key pair and registers the public key with LMS. Hardware fingerprint is supporting/versioned identity evidence; MAC address is never the sole device identity.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Enrollment and grants can bind to cryptographic identity. Major identity change requires controlled rehost rather than silent rebinding.

docs.title: ADR-006 — Separate License and Release Signing Keys
docs.text: Status: Approved

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use separate cryptographic key purposes for license/grant signing and software/model release signing.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Compromise or rotation of one trust purpose has reduced blast radius and clearer recovery procedures.

docs.title: ADR-007 — Signed Offline Request/Response
docs.text: Status: Approved

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Offline/air-gapped workflows use device-bound signed requests and centrally issued signed response packages linked by request ID and nonce. Relay devices are transport-only.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The same trust model works online and offline while limiting replay and preventing relay workstations from becoming signing authorities.

docs.title: ADR-008 — Production Human Authentication
docs.text: Status: Open Decision

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Development begins with username/password. Production enterprise deployments may require OIDC/SSO, MFA and customer identity-provider integration.

docs.title: Decision required
docs.text: Select the production authentication profile and deployment-specific identity-provider integration model before production readiness freeze. Authorization/RBAC is designed independently so the decision does not rewrite domain permissions.

docs.title: ADR-009 — Model Encryption and Key Wrapping
docs.text: Status: Open Security Decision

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text: Model artifacts are encrypted and signed. Entitlement controls authorization and device identity controls whether content-key material may be unwrapped/used.

docs.title: Decision required
docs.text: Finalize envelope-encryption algorithm, key hierarchy, KMS/HSM integration, per-device/per-deployment wrapping strategy, edge secure-storage expectations and rotation/recovery procedure. A universal model password is prohibited.

docs.title: ADR-010 — Release Package Format
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text: Traditional release bundle with signed manifest, application/UI/dependency artifacts, automated migration, health-check and rollback handlers. Linux shell handlers are first; Windows PowerShell equivalents remain future-compatible.

docs.title: Decision required
docs.text: Freeze archive/container format, canonical manifest serialization, compression, maximum package size, script execution sandboxing and artifact repository layout before Update Manager implementation is finalized.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The LMS is a modular enterprise control plane. Business truth is centralized; final authorization and installation enforcement remain local.

flowchart TB
    P[Admin / Customer Portal] --> API[Central LMS API]
    API --> REG[Registry & Enrollment]
    API --> ENT[Entitlement Engine]
    API --> POL[Policy Engine]
    API --> CAP[Capacity Service]
    API --> MKT[Marketplace]
    API --> REL[Release / OTA]
    API --> LIFE[Lifecycle / Renewal]
    API --> AUD[Audit & Reporting]
    ENT --> SIGN[Protected Signing Service]
    POL --> SIGN
    REL --> AR[(Artifact Repository)]
    API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    API -->|Online| EDGE[Edge / Server]
    API -->|Signed request-response| RELAY[Authorized Relay]
    RELAY --> EDGE
    EDGE --> ID[Device Identity]
    EDGE --> LA[License Agent]
    EDGE --> LC[Local Capacity Engine]
    EDGE --> UM[Update Manager]
    EDGE --> RT[Analytics Runtime]

docs.title: Responsibility split
docs.text:
• Entitlement Engine: what the customer owns.
  • Policy Engine: under what conditions it may be used.
  • Capacity Engine: what the hardware can run safely.
  • Release/OTA: which software/model artifacts are installed.
  • License Agent: whether the feature may execute.

docs.title: Artifact Storage Architecture
docs.text: PostgreSQL stores transactional metadata, references, hashes, signatures, compatibility and deployment state. Large application/model binaries must not be stored as normal PostgreSQL blobs.

docs.title: Storage abstraction
docs.text:
Release / Model Service
        ↓
Artifact Repository Interface
        ├── SaaS: S3-compatible object storage
        └── Customer-hosted: MinIO or approved local repository

docs.title: Stored metadata
docs.text: Database records include artifact ID, release/model association, URI/reference, size, content hash, signature/key ID, encryption profile, creation/publish state and retention metadata.

docs.title: Integrity
docs.text: Artifact bytes are immutable after publication. Replacement requires a new artifact/release identity. The edge verifies manifest signature and content hash before installation/decryption.

docs.title: Signing separation
docs.text: Artifact storage is not a signing authority. Signing keys remain in the protected signing boundary; the repository stores only signed outputs and verification metadata.

docs.title: Configuration & Policy Hierarchy
docs.text: The platform must resolve configuration deterministically across platform, product, customer, site and device scopes.

docs.title: Resolution order
docs.text:
Platform Default
    ↓
Product Override
    ↓
Customer / Entitlement Override
    ↓
Site Override
    ↓
Device Override

Only explicitly allowed policy keys may be overridden at lower scopes. Security minimums may be marked non-relaxable.

docs.title: Policy domains
docs.text:
• offline authorization duration
  • grace duration
  • trial duration and eligibility
  • release channel eligibility
  • automatic/manual OTA mode
  • maintenance window
  • rollback behavior
  • model-only update permission
  • concurrency limits
  • notification preferences
  • audit retention
  • capacity override policy

docs.title: Example resolved policy
docs.text:
{
  "offline_days": 7,
  "grace_days": 7,
  "trial_days": 14,
  "ota_mode": "auto",
  "release_channel": "stable",
  "maintenance_window": {"start": "01:00", "end": "03:00", "timezone": "site"},
  "auto_rollback": true,
  "model_only_updates": true
}

docs.title: Governance
docs.text: Every resolved policy response should include source metadata so operators can see which scope supplied each effective value. Changes to sensitive policy keys are audited.

docs.title: SaaS
docs.text:
• Multi-tenant logical isolation.
  • Phase 1: single-primary baseline with monitoring, automated backups and documented recovery.
  • Design remains HA-ready.

docs.title: Customer-hosted
docs.text:
• Same LMS codebase.
  • Isolated deployment.
  • Manual LMS package upgrade acceptable initially.
  • HA is optional enterprise capability.

docs.title: Delivery routes
docs.text:
1. Online API.
  2. Assisted offline relay.
  3. Fully air-gapped signed request/response.

All use the same signed artifact trust model.

docs.title: Capacity reassessment after hardware/workload change
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant C as Central Capacity
    participant L as Local Capacity
    participant A as Admin
    D->>C: New inventory/resource/workload snapshot
    C->>C: Recalculate using benchmark profile
    C-->>A: Pass/warning/fail + recommendations
    A->>D: Choose approved configuration if adjustment needed
    D->>L: Reassess actual local combined workload

docs.title: Online software/model update
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as LMS Deployment
    participant D as Update Manager
    participant R as Runtime
    L-->>D: Deployment target + signed release-set manifest
    D->>D: Preflight license/compatibility/disk/capacity
    D->>L: Fetch only missing artifacts/models
    D->>D: Verify signatures/hashes
    D->>D: Preserve known-good release set
    D->>D: Stage + migrate
    D->>R: Restart/start target services
    R-->>D: Health result
    alt Health OK
      D->>D: Commit target release set
      D-->>L: Installation receipt
    else Health failed
      D->>D: Roll back coherent previous release set
      D-->>L: Failure/rollback receipt
    end

docs.title: Offline software/model update
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant O as Relay/Media
    participant L as LMS
    D->>O: Export request + installed release/model inventory
    O->>L: Import request
    L->>L: Resolve minimal delta bundle
    L-->>O: Signed release set + only missing artifacts
    O-->>D: Import package
    D->>D: Verify + preflight + stage + migrate + health-check
    alt Success
      D->>D: Commit
    else Failure
      D->>D: Rollback
    end
    D-->>O: Signed installation receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile

docs.title: Renewal for offline device
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Customer
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing Service
    participant O as Offline Relay
    participant D as Device
    U->>L: Renewal request / commercial approval
    L->>S: Sign superseding grant revision
    S-->>L: Signed renewed grant
    L-->>O: Export response package
    O-->>D: Controlled-media transfer
    D->>D: Verify revision, binding, term, supersession
    D-->>O: Signed acceptance receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile receipt

docs.title: Device replacement / rehost
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Authorized Admin
    participant O as Old Device
    participant N as New/Changed Device
    participant L as LMS
    A->>L: Submit replacement/rehost request
    N->>L: Register new cryptographic identity/fingerprint
    L->>L: Validate ownership + approval + allocation
    L->>L: Retire/suspend old binding
    L->>L: Reassign/return allocation
    L-->>N: New device-bound superseding grant
    N->>N: Verify and activate
    N-->>L: Acceptance receipt

docs.title: Device transfer
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Requester
    actor B as Approver
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Device
    A->>L: Request customer/site transfer
    L->>L: Validate current rights and target ownership
    L-->>B: Maker-checker approval request
    B->>L: Approve
    L->>L: Supersede invalid old grants + update ownership/site assignments
    L-->>D: New valid grant/policy state
    D-->>L: Acceptance receipt

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Admin
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Connected Device
    participant O as Air-gapped Device
    A->>L: Revoke grant/device
    L->>L: Record revocation + superseding state
    L-->>D: Deliver at sync/check-in
    D->>D: Enforce revoke
    Note over O,L: Air-gapped enforcement waits for signed import or offline expiry

docs.title: Failed update and rollback
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Update Manager
    participant R as Runtime
    L-->>D: Target release set
    D->>D: Verify + stage + install
    D->>R: Health check
    R-->>D: FAIL
    D->>D: Restore previous app/plugin/UI/model/config set
    D->>R: Verify rollback health
    alt Rollback healthy
      D-->>L: Rolled-back receipt
    else Rollback failed
      D-->>L: Critical failure receipt / escalate
    end

docs.title: Check-in freshness expiry
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant L as License Agent
    D->>L: Runtime authorization check
    L->>L: Compare last successful authorized check-in to policy
    alt Fresh
      L-->>D: Continue
    else Stale but grace/revalidation policy allows restricted state
      L-->>D: Restricted/grace + recovery path
    else Authorization no longer valid
      L-->>D: Disable unauthorized analytics; preserve recovery/diagnostics where allowed
    end

docs.title: Commercial expiry and grace
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Runtime
    participant L as License Agent
    R->>L: Feature authorization request
    L->>L: Evaluate commercial valid_until independently from offline freshness
    alt Commercial term active
      L-->>R: Allow subject to other gates
    else Expired and grace active
      L-->>R: Grace/restricted behavior per policy
    else Expired and grace ended
      L-->>R: Deny analytics execution; keep recovery/diagnostics where allowed
    end

docs.title: State Machines
docs.text: State transitions are explicit, auditable and transactional where business integrity requires it.

docs.title: Device
docs.text:
PENDING -> REGISTERED -> ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> RETIRED
                         |
                         +-> REHOST_REQUIRED

docs.title: Grant / License
docs.text:
DRAFT -> ISSUED -> DELIVERED -> ACCEPTED -> ACTIVE -> GRACE -> EXPIRED
                                               |
                                               +-> REVOKED

ISSUED does not mean the device has received it. DELIVERED does not mean the device accepted it.

docs.title: Trial
docs.text:
ELIGIBLE -> REQUESTED -> ISSUED -> ACTIVE -> EXPIRED
                                      |
                                      +-> CONVERTED

Trial time begins when activation succeeds, not when the request or grant is issued.

docs.title: Purchase Request
docs.text:
REQUESTED -> REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PAID/COMMERCIAL_CONFIRMED -> GRANT_ISSUED
                  |
                  +-> REJECTED

A purchase request or catalog entry never authorizes execution by itself.

docs.title: Offline Request / Response
docs.text:
CREATED -> EXPORTED -> RECEIVED -> APPROVED -> RESPONSE_ISSUED -> IMPORTED -> RECONCILED
                           |            |
                           |            +-> REJECTED
                           +-> EXPIRED

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
AVAILABLE -> DOWNLOADED/IMPORTED -> VERIFIED -> STAGED -> INSTALLING -> HEALTH_CHECK -> ACTIVE
                                                              |             |
                                                              |             +-> ROLLED_BACK
                                                              +-> FAILED

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text:
DUE_SOON -> REQUESTED -> APPROVED_GRANT_ISSUED -> DELIVERED_IMPORTED -> ACCEPTED_ACTIVE
                |                   |                     |
                +-> REJECTED       +-> FAILED            +-> FAILED
                                                            |
                                                            +-> EXPIRED_RESTRICTED

docs.title: Governance rule
docs.text: Any implementation-specific state must map cleanly to these business states or be documented as an internal sub-state. UI/API must not collapse distinct business milestones that affect support or audit.

docs.title: Central
docs.text: Commercial authorization is central, but signing private keys are outside normal application storage.

docs.title: Edge
docs.text: The edge verifies signature, binding, dates, revision, dependencies, offline freshness, package/model integrity and local capacity.

docs.title: Assisted offline
docs.text:
The relay is transport-only and has no signing authority.

    participant R as Relay
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing Service

    R-->>D: Controlled-media transfer
    D->>D: Verify, install, activate

docs.title: Backend Engineering
docs.text:
Baseline stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Pydantic, React/Vite/TypeScript.

Start as a modular monolith with explicit domains: identity/access, customers/sites, devices/enrollment, catalog, entitlements, policy, grants, capacity, marketplace, releases, artifacts, deployments, renewals, offline exchange, telemetry, notifications, audit and signing gateway.

• All business tables carry customer/tenant ownership directly or through an enforceable FK path.
  • Allocation updates and grant supersession occur in a single business transaction where possible.
  • Idempotency keys have unique constraints at the workflow boundary.
  • Mutable business objects carry revision/version columns for optimistic concurrency.
  • Audit events are append-only.
  • UTC is used for persisted timestamps; site timezone is display/scheduling context only.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text: Category Typical HTTP Examples validation 400/422 malformed scope, invalid quantity authentication 401 invalid user/device credential authorization 403 cross-tenant access, unapproved override not_found 404 device/release does not exist in caller scope conflict 409 duplicate allocation, stale revision, rehost required rate_limit 429 enrollment or request abuse protection dependency 424 required base grant/model/runtime unavailable temporary 503 signing gateway/artifact service unavailable

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Error codes are documented and never repurposed.
  • retryable reflects workflow semantics, not only HTTP class.
  • Security-sensitive reasons may be intentionally generalized externally while full detail is written to audit/secure logs.
  • Offline import errors must be deterministic enough for field operators to recover without site debugging.

docs.title: Database Indexing, Transactions & Concurrency
docs.text: Tier-1 reliability depends on explicit concurrency behaviour, not only schema shape.

docs.title: Transaction boundaries
docs.text:
Use one database transaction for operations where partial success would violate commercial truth, including: - entitlement-pool reallocation across multiple devices - grant revision + supersession record creation - renewal term update + grant issuance record preparation - device decommission + allocation return - approval execution state transitions

External calls such as signing and artifact storage should use an outbox/saga-style pattern when they cannot participate in the DB transaction.

docs.title: Optimistic concurrency
docs.text: Mutable aggregates carry revision or version. Update commands include expected revision. A mismatch returns a conflict rather than overwriting concurrent changes.

docs.title: Initial index strategy
docs.text:
• unique(customer_id, external_reference) where integration keys apply
  • unique(device_id, active key status constraint)
  • index(customer_id, status) on customer-scoped collections
  • index(device_id, collected_at desc) for inventory/snapshots
  • unique(entitlement_id, feature_id, active pool identity) as model permits
  • index(grants: device_id, status, valid_until)
  • unique(grant_id, revision)
  • index(capacity_assessments: device_id, assessed_at desc)
  • unique(feature_id, version) and unique(model_id, version)
  • index(deployment_targets: job_id, status)
  • index(audit_events: customer_id, occurred_at desc) and object lookup indexes

Exact indexes must be validated against production-like query plans before launch.

docs.title: Idempotency storage
docs.text: Persist key, operation, request hash, response reference, created_at and expiry. Same key + different request hash is rejected.

docs.title: Database Migration Policy
docs.text: Database evolution must be safe across SaaS and customer-hosted deployments.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Alembic is the only supported schema migration path.
  • Production schema changes are reviewed like application code.
  • Destructive migrations are never combined with the first release that stops using the old field/table.
  • Prefer expand-and-contract for risky changes.
  • Migrations must be idempotent at deployment orchestration level and never require manual SQL at customer sites.

docs.title: Expand-and-contract example
docs.text:
Release N: add new nullable column/table + dual-read/write where needed
Release N+1: backfill/verify + switch reads
Release N+2: stop writing old field
Release N+3: remove old field after support window

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Before Stable promotion, verify whether application rollback is compatible with the migrated schema. If schema rollback is unsafe, the release must use backward-compatible migration design rather than assuming DB downgrade.

docs.title: Customer-hosted
docs.text: Each release package declares supported source schema versions and target schema version. Update Manager blocks unsupported upgrade jumps and provides a clear required intermediate version.

docs.title: Backend Modules — Detailed Responsibilities
docs.text: This page defines the initial modular-monolith boundaries. Modules may share one deployable process and database while maintaining explicit ownership and service interfaces.

Must not: - own commercial entitlement logic - directly mutate device grants

docs.title: Customer, Site & Topology
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - customer lifecycle - site lifecycle and timezone - device ownership relationships - device-to-site assignments including multi-site server topology - transfer/decommission coordination

Key invariants: - a device has one commercial owner at a time - site assignments are explicit and auditable - transfer never silently overwrites previous ownership

docs.text:
Responsibilities: - enrollment authorization creation - single-use/short-lived enrollment token validation - public-key registration - fingerprint version validation - duplicate/prior-registration detection - initial hardware inventory capture

docs.text: Responsibilities: - products - features - dependencies - compatibility metadata - marketplace visibility - release/model associations

docs.title: Entitlements

Responsibilities: - commercial rights - subscription/perpetual term - entitlement pools - update-right policy - ERP synchronization boundary

docs.title: Allocation
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - distribute pooled quantities to device/site scopes - validate total quantity - support reallocation - create a stable snapshot used for grant generation

docs.text:
Responsibilities: - construct canonical device-bound grant payload - resolve dependencies and constraints - revision and supersession - signing request - issuance record - delivery/reconciliation state

Responsibilities: - inventory normalization - benchmark lookup - current+proposed workload calculation - feasibility result - recommended alternatives - assessment evidence/versioning

Must never mutate commercial entitlement automatically.

docs.title: Capacity Management
docs.text: Capacity management answers what this hardware can run at the target performance, independently from what the customer commercially owns.

docs.title: Four independent states
docs.text:
A feature/device combination must keep these states separate:

  1. Licensed — commercial right exists.
  2. Compatible — OS/runtime/hardware/dependency requirements are satisfied.
  3. Capacity Validated — combined workload meets the performance target or an approved warning policy.
  4. Installed / Healthy — required application/model components are installed and healthy.

A feature activates only when all required gates pass.

docs.title: Authority model
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine performs advisory pre-assessment using reported inventory, workload definitions and approved benchmark profiles.

Local Capacity Engine performs the authoritative activation check using current drivers, resources, active streams, installed versions and actual local runtime conditions.

docs.title: Core process
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Collect stable inventory] --> B[Check compatibility]
    B --> C[Describe current + proposed workloads]
    C --> D[Select approved benchmark profiles]
    D --> E[Calculate combined resource budget]
    E --> F[Compare against target/headroom policy]
    F --> G{PASS / WARNING / FAIL}
    G -->|PASS| H[Recommend activation]
    G -->|WARNING| I[Recommend constrained configuration]
    G -->|FAIL| J[Recommend alternatives / hardware change]
    H --> K[Local authoritative recheck]
    I --> K
    J --> K
    K --> L[Monitor runtime and reassess on change]

docs.title: Non-negotiable rules
docs.text:
• Capacity never silently reduces purchased entitlement.
  • Licensed camera/feature quantity is not itself a capacity calculation.
  • Existing and proposed workloads are evaluated together.
  • Central advice may become stale; local activation remains authoritative.
  • Capacity recommendations are explicit and operator-selectable.
  • Benchmark evidence is versioned and governed.
  • Runtime changes can invalidate an old assessment.

docs.title: Authority split
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine performs advisory pre-assessment using reported inventory and benchmark profiles.

Local Capacity Engine is authoritative for actual activation because it sees current runtime, active streams, drivers, local resources and installed components.

docs.title: Activation gate
docs.text: A feature may activate only when: 1. grant is valid 2. compatibility constraints pass 3. required package/model is installed and healthy 4. local combined-workload capacity validation passes for the selected configuration

docs.title: Recommendation mode
docs.text:
The engine recommends; it does not silently reconfigure commercial use.

Example for licensed People Counting 8 + PPE 4 when full combined workload fails: - PC 8 + PPE 2 - PC 4 + PPE 4 - reduce FPS/resolution - select optimized model/runtime - move one workload to another device - upgrade hardware

The customer/admin explicitly chooses an allowed recommendation. Purchased entitlement remains People Counting 8 + PPE 4 unless a commercial change is separately made.

docs.title: Confidence and evidence
docs.text: Assessment records should include benchmark profile/version, inventory version, workload inputs, result, limiting resource, recommendations and confidence/evidence quality.

docs.title: Benchmark Profile Governance
docs.text: Benchmark data is production engineering evidence. It requires versioning, ownership and release discipline.

docs.title: Benchmark profile dimensions
docs.text: A profile may be keyed by: - hardware class/model - accelerator/GPU architecture and VRAM - driver/runtime stack - feature/model/version - resolution/FPS/codec - decode path - inference backend and precision - concurrent workloads - measured latency/FPS/utilization/headroom

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
DRAFT -> VALIDATING -> APPROVED -> ACTIVE -> SUPERSEDED -> RETIRED

Only APPROVED/ACTIVE benchmark profiles may drive production recommendations.

docs.title: Evidence requirements
docs.text: Each benchmark profile records: - benchmark version - test hardware identity/class - software/runtime versions - test dataset/workload definition - warm-up period - sample duration - measured throughput/latency - CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/decode utilization - temperature/throttling observations - target/headroom thresholds - test date and owner - approval status

docs.title: Matching
docs.text: The Capacity Engine chooses the closest valid profile using explicit compatibility rules. It must not silently use a materially different hardware/runtime profile without reducing confidence or marking the result unsupported.

docs.title: Confidence
docs.text: Suggested confidence categories: - high: exact or validated-equivalent profile - medium: approved near-match with bounded interpolation - low: weak match; recommendation only, activation may require local empirical validation - unsupported: no valid evidence

docs.title: Headroom
docs.text:
Capacity results should expose remaining headroom for limiting resources when measurable. Example: GPU compute headroom 14%, VRAM headroom 22%, CPU headroom 35%.

Thresholds are product/benchmark policy, not hard-coded globally.

docs.title: Default decision mode
docs.text: The Capacity Engine recommends a feasible configuration. The customer/admin explicitly selects the configuration. The platform must never silently lower camera count, FPS, resolution or purchased entitlement.

docs.title: PASS
docs.text: Activation may proceed if all licensing, compatibility, installation and health gates also pass.

docs.title: WARNING
docs.text: Activation may proceed only if product policy permits warning acceptance. The selected configuration and warning acknowledgement are audited.

docs.title: FAIL
docs.text: Normal activation is blocked. The system presents recommendations such as reduced active workload, lower FPS/resolution, alternative model/runtime, moving workloads, second device or hardware upgrade.

docs.title: Exceptional override
docs.text:
If the company chooses to support a capacity override for exceptional cases, it is a privileged maker-checker action and must: - never change the commercial entitlement - capture requester, approver, reason and expiry - bind to a specific device/workload/release/model context - be time-limited or revision-limited - generate an audit event - be visible in support/operations views - automatically become invalid when material hardware/runtime/workload state changes

A capacity override must not bypass hard technical incompatibility such as unsupported architecture, missing required runtime or invalid package/model signature.

docs.title: Recommendation selection
docs.text: The selected recommendation becomes part of the activation/deployment record so later support can distinguish licensed rights from the operator-selected active configuration.

docs.title: Inventory & Benchmarking
docs.text: Stable inventory and dynamic resource snapshots are stored separately.

docs.title: Stable inventory
docs.text:
Collect at minimum:

  • CPU model, architecture, physical/logical cores and relevant frequency/capability data
  • RAM total and configured limits
  • GPU model/architecture, VRAM and relevant compute capability
  • accelerators such as Jetson/NPU where applicable
  • storage total/free/filesystem/health evidence
  • OS distribution/version, kernel
  • GPU/accelerator drivers
  • CUDA, TensorRT, DeepStream and product runtime versions
  • camera workload descriptors: count, resolution, FPS, codec/decode requirements
  • installed services, application releases and model inventory

docs.title: Dynamic snapshots
docs.text:
Capture separately:

  • available RAM
  • free disk
  • GPU/accelerator utilization
  • temperature/throttling
  • active streams
  • active workloads
  • other runtime pressure signals needed by the local Capacity Engine

docs.title: Benchmark profiles
docs.text:
Capacity decisions use measured, versioned benchmark profiles across:

  • hardware class
  • analytics model/version
  • resolution
  • FPS
  • inference backend
  • decoder/pipeline
  • concurrent workloads
  • target latency/FPS/SLA

Instantaneous utilization alone is not a benchmark.

Every assessment must record the benchmark profile/version and inventory/workload inputs used so the result can be reproduced and audited.

docs.title: Combined Workload Planning
docs.text:
Capacity planning evaluates the complete active and proposed workload, not individual feature quotas in isolation.

flowchart TD
    A[Collect Inventory] --> B[Compatibility Check]
    B --> C[Load Existing Workloads]
    C --> D[Add Proposed Workload]
    D --> E[Resolve Approved Benchmark Profiles]
    E --> F[Calculate Combined CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/Decode/Disk/Thermal Budget]
    F --> G[Apply Performance + Headroom Targets]
    G --> H{PASS / WARNING / FAIL}
    H -->|PASS| I[Recommend Activation]
    H -->|WARNING| J[Recommend Approved Alternatives]
    H -->|FAIL| K[Block Normal Activation + Recommend Alternatives]
    I --> L[Local Authoritative Recheck]
    J --> L
    K --> L

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Commercial entitlement:

People Counting = 8 cameras
PPE = 4 cameras

The Capacity Engine does not assume 8 + 4 = 12 cameras is feasible. It evaluates the real combined workload using model/runtime/resolution/FPS/decode and concurrency evidence.

If the selected workload does not meet target performance, recommendations may include:

  • People Counting 8 + PPE 2
  • People Counting 4 + PPE 4
  • lower FPS
  • lower resolution
  • different decode path
  • optimized model/runtime
  • move a workload to another device
  • deploy a second device
  • hardware upgrade

The operator/customer chooses an allowed configuration. Purchased entitlement remains unchanged.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A capacity assessment should return:

  • result: pass / warning / fail / stale
  • limiting resource(s)
  • compatibility blockers
  • benchmark profile/version
  • workload hash/input summary
  • expected/observed headroom
  • confidence/evidence quality
  • recommendations
  • assessment timestamp and freshness
  • whether local revalidation is required

docs.title: Reassessment & Runtime Monitoring
docs.text: Capacity is not a one-time registration result. Assessments become stale when relevant conditions change.

docs.title: Mandatory reassessment triggers
docs.text:
• hardware inventory change
  • GPU/accelerator or driver change
  • CUDA/TensorRT/DeepStream/runtime change
  • application/feature release change
  • model version change
  • camera count/resolution/FPS/codec change
  • new feature activation
  • feature deactivation that changes combined workload
  • site-to-device workload movement
  • benchmark profile superseded by a materially different approved profile
  • repeated runtime degradation or thermal throttling

docs.title: Runtime monitoring signals
docs.text: Where available, monitor: - achieved inference/processed FPS - p95/p99 inference latency - dropped/late frames - CPU/GPU utilization - VRAM/RAM pressure - decoder utilization - temperature/throttling - service health/restarts - active stream count

docs.title: Drift handling
docs.text:
Healthy -> Warning -> Reassess -> Recommendation / Operator Action
                     |
                     +-> Critical degradation -> protect service / fail feature according to runtime safety policy

Runtime degradation does not rewrite entitlement. It may trigger a new capacity assessment and recommendation.

docs.title: Assessment freshness
docs.text: Each assessment records inventory version, resource snapshot timestamp, workload hash, benchmark version and software/model versions. If any required input changes, the previous assessment becomes stale.

docs.title: Central vs local drift
docs.text: Central LMS may show an advisory result based on last reported evidence. The local Capacity Engine remains authoritative for activation because it can detect current real conditions.

docs.title: Telemetry integration
docs.text: Capacity history may be forwarded to telemetry/analytics for trend analysis, but transactional activation state stays in the operational LMS/device state model.

docs.title: Capacity Status Model
docs.text: Capacity-related states must remain separate from commercial licensing and installation state. UI, API and audit records must not collapse them into one boolean.

docs.title: Independent status dimensions
docs.text:
Dimension Meaning Example states Licensed Customer/device has valid commercial authorization not_entitled, entitled, grant_pending, grant_active Compatible Software/model can technically run on this platform/runtime unknown, compatible, incompatible, blocked_dependency Capacity validated Combined workload is expected to meet the defined performance target not_assessed, pass, warning, fail, stale Installed / healthy Required application/model components are present and healthy not_installed, staged, healthy, degraded, failed

These dimensions are evaluated independently and then combined for activation.

docs.title: Activation rule
docs.text:
Licensed
AND Compatible
AND Capacity Validated
AND Installed / Healthy
= Feature may activate

A commercial entitlement can be valid even when the device is incompatible or under-capacity. Capacity failure never removes purchased entitlement.

docs.title: Capacity result semantics
docs.text:
PASS — benchmark evidence and current local conditions meet target with required headroom.

WARNING — workload is likely feasible but headroom/confidence is below preferred target, or the operator must choose an allowed lower-load configuration.

FAIL — the selected combined workload does not meet the minimum activation target.

STALE — the assessment is no longer valid because inventory, runtime, model, workload or benchmark policy changed.

docs.title: Reason-code examples
docs.text:
CAP_GPU_VRAM_INSUFFICIENT
CAP_GPU_COMPUTE_BELOW_TARGET
CAP_CPU_HEADROOM_LOW
CAP_RAM_HEADROOM_LOW
CAP_DISK_FREE_LOW
CAP_RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED
CAP_DRIVER_MISMATCH
CAP_DECODE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
CAP_COMBINED_WORKLOAD_EXCEEDS_PROFILE
CAP_BENCHMARK_PROFILE_MISSING
CAP_INVENTORY_STALE
CAP_RESOURCE_SNAPSHOT_STALE

Reason codes are stable machine-readable values and map to operator-safe recommendations.

docs.title: Workload Model
docs.text: Capacity planning is based on actual workload characteristics rather than licensed quantity alone.

docs.title: Workload dimensions
docs.text: A workload profile should capture, where relevant: - feature/capability code - analytics model ID and version - camera/input count - per-input resolution - FPS - codec - decode path (CPU/GPU/hardware decoder) - inference backend - precision - batching/concurrency - preprocessing/postprocessing cost class - retention/output pipeline impact where applicable - site assignment - required performance target such as minimum processed FPS or maximum latency

docs.title: Example workload
docs.text:
{
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "model_id": "ppe_detector",
  "model_version": "7.3.0",
  "site_id": "site_a",
  "inputs": {
    "camera_count": 4,
    "resolution": "1920x1080",
    "fps": 10,
    "codec": "h264",
    "decode_path": "gpu"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "backend": "tensorrt",
    "precision": "fp16"
  },
  "target": {
    "min_processed_fps": 9.5,
    "max_p95_latency_ms": 250
  }
}

docs.title: Combined workload budget
docs.text:
The Capacity Engine evaluates all active workloads plus the proposed workload together.

Existing workload A
+ Existing workload B
+ Proposed workload C
----------------------
Combined CPU / RAM / GPU / VRAM / decode / storage / thermal budget

Licensed quotas must not simply be added and treated as capacity.

docs.title: Multi-site devices
docs.text: For a device serving multiple sites, the workload model retains site attribution but capacity is evaluated at the shared device resource level. Site limits constrain commercial use; shared hardware capacity constrains actual concurrent execution.

docs.title: Workload identity
docs.text: Persist a stable workload profile or canonical workload hash so assessments can be reproduced and compared over time.

docs.title: Open Decisions
docs.text: Topic Status Production human authentication / SSO Open Exact model key wrapping / secure local key storage Security ADR required Telemetry privacy / opt-in / residency Open Final API schemas and error catalog Open Enterprise HA RTO/RPO Open

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text:
1. Trust foundation — identity, grant schema, verifier, enrollment.
  2. Registry & licensing — customer/site/device, entitlement pools, allocations, base activation.
  3. Hardware & capacity — inventory, snapshots, benchmark profiles, combined workload.
  4. Marketplace & release management — catalog, trials, purchase requests, package repository, Stable/LTS.
  5. Model OTA & deployment — encrypted models, model inventory, release sets, maintenance windows, rollback.
  6. Lifecycle — renewal, offline validity, grace, check-in, revocation, rehost, decommission.
  7. Hardening — VAPT, DR, operational runbooks, ERP sync, production readiness.

docs.title: Development Readiness Checklist
docs.text:
• Business outcome defined
  • Scope/non-goals clear
  • State machine documented
  • DB ownership and transaction boundaries known
  • API contracts drafted
  • Authorization/tenant scope defined
  • Offline behaviour defined
  • Failure and rollback defined
  • Audit events identified
  • Threats reviewed
  • Capacity impact considered
  • QA acceptance criteria written
  • ADR created for material design choices
  • Team ownership agreed

docs.title: Initial Work Breakdown Structure
docs.text: The following epics provide a practical starting backlog aligned with architecture boundaries.

docs.title: Epic A — Platform foundation
docs.text:
• repository/project scaffolding
  • configuration/secrets abstraction
  • DB/Alembic baseline
  • common ID/time/error/audit primitives
  • development username/password auth
  • RBAC/scope enforcement

docs.title: Epic B — Customer, site and device
docs.text:
• customer/site CRUD
  • device ownership/site assignments
  • enrollment authorization
  • device registration
  • hardware inventory upload
  • transfer/rehost/decommission

docs.title: Epic C — Licensing core
docs.text:
• product/feature catalog
  • entitlement pools
  • allocations/reallocation transaction
  • policy resolution
  • grant canonicalization/signing integration
  • local License Agent contract
  • renewal/check-in/grace/revocation

docs.title: Epic D — Capacity
docs.text:
• inventory normalization
  • benchmark profile model
  • workload model
  • central assessment
  • local assessment contract
  • recommendation engine

docs.title: Epic E — Marketplace
docs.text:
• feature listing/detail
  • eligibility
  • dynamic trial policies/campaigns
  • purchase-request workflow
  • approval screens

docs.title: Epic F — Release & OTA
docs.text:
• artifact repository abstraction
  • release/model manifests
  • release channels
  • deployment jobs/targets
  • auto/manual policy and maintenance window
  • edge Update Manager
  • health check and release-set rollback

docs.title: Epic G — Offline operations
docs.text:
• request export schema
  • central import validation
  • minimal bundle builder
  • signed response package
  • local import
  • receipt export/reconciliation

docs.title: Epic H — Governance & operations
docs.text:
• notifications
  • audit explorer
  • monitoring/metrics
  • backups/restore
  • VAPT gates
  • ERP adapter contract

Each epic should be decomposed into vertical slices that include backend, edge/UI, tests, audit and documentation rather than deferring integration until the end.

docs.title: Edge / Application Engineering
docs.text:
The local product remains operational without continuous internet for its authorized offline period.

Core local components: Device Identity Agent, Hardware Inventory Agent, Local Capacity Engine, License Agent, Feature Update Manager and Analytics Runtime/Product Adapter.

docs.title: Identity material
docs.text:
• device-generated asymmetric key pair
  • centrally registered public key
  • versioned hardware fingerprint
  • MAC/network identifiers as supporting evidence only

docs.title: Fingerprint policy
docs.text:
Fingerprint comparison is weighted/tolerant rather than exact equality.

Minor changes normally trigger compatibility revalidation but do not require rehost: - RAM upgrade/replacement - storage replacement - NIC replacement - added accelerator where identity remains stable

Major changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED: - motherboard replacement - device private key loss/recreation - multiple core identity attributes change beyond tolerance

docs.title: Rehost flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Identity mismatch detected] --> B{Minor or Major?}
    B -->|Minor| C[Revalidate compatibility/capacity]
    C --> D[Continue with audit]
    B -->|Major| E[REHOST_REQUIRED]
    E --> F[Admin / maker-checker approval]
    F --> G[Register replacement identity]
    G --> H[Issue superseding device grant]
    H --> I[Return old allocation / retire old binding]

docs.title: License Agent
docs.text:
The local License Agent verifies signature, device/product binding, revision/supersession, commercial validity, offline freshness, dependencies, limits, anti-replay/rollback state and trusted/last-known time.

Authorization must be enforced at runtime service boundaries, not only by hiding UI options.

docs.title: Local Component Interfaces
docs.text: Local components must interact through explicit contracts so product teams do not bypass licensing or update controls.

docs.title: License Agent API
docs.text:
Suggested local-only interface:

GET  /local/v1/license/status
POST /local/v1/license/import
POST /local/v1/license/check
GET  /local/v1/features/effective

license/check inputs feature, requested quantity/scope, product context and optional workload reference; output is allow/deny/restricted with reason code and effective grant revision.

docs.title: Capacity Engine API
docs.text:
POST /local/v1/capacity/assess
GET  /local/v1/capacity/latest

Inputs include current resource snapshot, existing workloads, proposed workloads and benchmark profile version. It returns pass/warning/fail plus recommendations; it never changes purchased rights.

docs.title: Update Manager API
docs.text:
POST /local/v1/releases/import
POST /local/v1/releases/install
POST /local/v1/releases/rollback
GET  /local/v1/releases/status
GET  /local/v1/models/inventory

Only the Update Manager may activate a release set. Product services must not unpack arbitrary marketplace files directly.

docs.title: Runtime adapter contract
docs.text: Analytics services must ask the License Agent for authorization at actual execution boundaries. UI state may mirror authorization but cannot be the enforcement layer.

docs.title: Local persistence
docs.text: Protected local state should include accepted grant revision/sequence, last-known trusted time, current release set, rollback release set, installed model inventory and latest signed receipt queue.

docs.title: Offline & Air-Gapped Workflows
docs.text: Offline support is a first-class product path, not an exception.

docs.title: Request package contains
docs.text:
• request_id and nonce
  • device identity/public-key reference
  • current grant revisions
  • installed release/model inventory
  • hardware inventory version and relevant workload
  • requested operation: activation, trial, renewal, release update, model update
  • device signature over canonical request payload

docs.title: Response package contains
docs.text:
• request_id/nonce binding
  • signed grant revision(s) where applicable
  • release-set manifest
  • only required/missing artifacts
  • encrypted model artifacts if required
  • signatures/hashes
  • expiry/import policy

docs.title: Local import order
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read Package] --> B[Verify package signature/hash]
    B --> C[Verify request_id + nonce binding]
    C --> D[Verify device/product scope]
    D --> E[Reject replay / stale revision]
    E --> F[Resolve grant and dependencies]
    F --> G[Capacity re-check]
    G --> H[Stage release set]
    H --> I[Health check]
    I -->|Pass| J[Commit + activate]
    I -->|Fail| K[Rollback]
    J --> L[Generate signed receipt]

Revocation cannot be instantaneous on a fully air-gapped device; it becomes effective when new signed state is imported or when existing offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Release Set & Rollback Contract
docs.text: A deployment is defined as a coherent release set rather than an isolated application file.

docs.title: Example release set
docs.text:
release_set_id: rs_2026_10_18_01
application: 5.8.0
features:
  ppe: 4.2.1
ui: 2.5.0
runtime: 3.7.0
models:
  ppe_detector: 7.3.0
config_schema: 6

docs.title: Update transaction
docs.text:
1. Preflight compatibility, disk and policy checks.
  2. Preserve current known-good release set.
  3. Fetch/import only missing artifacts.
  4. Verify every artifact.
  5. Run automated config/database migrations.
  6. Start target services.
  7. Run warm-up and health probes.
  8. Atomically mark release set active.
  9. On failure restore previous release set and compatible config/model state.

Retention: compress and retain 2–3 known-good sets where storage permits; immediately previous known-good set is mandatory.

docs.title: Update Manager
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Receive Release Set] --> B[Verify Signatures & Hashes]
    B --> C[Check OS / Architecture]
    C --> D[Check Disk / Dependencies]
    D --> E[Check License]
    E --> F[Check Capacity]
    F --> G[Preserve Known-Good Version]
    G --> H[Stage]
    H --> I[Run Migrations]
    I --> J[Restart Services]
    J --> K[Health Check]
    K -->|Pass| L[Commit]
    K -->|Fail| M[Rollback]

No normal production release should depend on manual site migration.

docs.title: Developer Setup
docs.text: This page defines the baseline local development workflow for the LMS handbook and the future application repositories.

docs.title: Required tools
docs.text:
• Python 3.12
  • Git
  • PostgreSQL client/server for backend development
  • Node.js LTS for React/Vite portal development
  • MkDocs dependencies from requirements.txt for handbook work

docs.title: Handbook preview
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Development principles
docs.text:
• Use synthetic data only.
  • Never use production signing keys in development.
  • Keep configuration outside source code.
  • Run migrations through Alembic only.
  • Use feature flags/policy configuration rather than ad-hoc code branches for customer exceptions.
  • Keep edge interfaces backward-compatible across supported release windows.

docs.title: Before opening a PR
docs.text:
• run unit/integration tests for affected code
  • run mkdocs build --strict for documentation changes
  • update ADRs when architecture changed
  • verify no secrets/customer data are included
  • document rollback/migration impact

docs.title: Engineering Change Control
docs.text: Tier-1 governance requires traceability from business decision to code and production release.

docs.title: Change classes
docs.text: Class Example Required controls Standard bug fix, docs, non-risk refactor PR + tests + review Architecture new module, trust boundary, schema model ADR + architecture review + PR Security-sensitive signing, auth, import parser, model protection security review + tests + VAPT scope review Commercial-policy entitlement, expiry, trial, renewal rules product/commercial approval + regression tests Emergency critical security/production issue expedited approval + complete post-change review

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text: Every material production change should be traceable to requirement/issue, design/ADR where relevant, pull request, CI evidence, release identifier and deployment/audit event.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Examples Handling baseline Public approved public product docs may be shared externally Internal architecture, roadmaps, operational metrics company/internal access Confidential customer/device inventories, entitlement details, audit exports restricted need-to-know Highly Restricted signing private keys, credentials, model content keys, incident secrets dedicated protected systems; never normal docs/logs

docs.title: Repository rule
docs.text: This private handbook may contain Internal and selected Confidential design information, but never secrets, credentials, private keys, decrypted proprietary models or raw sensitive incident/customer exports.

docs.title: Logging rule
docs.text: Logs should contain identifiers and references, not full sensitive payloads unless explicitly approved for a secure diagnostic channel.

docs.title: Export rule
docs.text: Audit/report exports must enforce caller scope and may require additional approval depending on customer data sensitivity.

docs.title: Engineering Decision Gates
docs.text: Large work items pass explicit decision gates before production.

docs.title: Gate 0 — Problem/Sponsor
docs.text: Business outcome, owner, scope and success criteria approved.

docs.title: Gate 1 — Architecture Ready
docs.text: Trust boundaries, state model, data ownership, APIs and ADR impact reviewed.

docs.title: Gate 2 — Development Ready
docs.text: Stories, acceptance criteria, dependencies, test approach and environment needs are ready.

docs.title: Gate 3 — Release Candidate
docs.text: Code complete, migrations/upgrades/rollback tested, security scans complete, docs current.

docs.title: Gate 4 — Production Approval
docs.text: QA evidence, release notes, known issues, VAPT/security disposition, rollout/rollback plan and approvals complete.

docs.title: Gate 5 — Post-Release
docs.text:
Deployment health, incidents, customer feedback, metrics and follow-up actions reviewed.

Gate evidence should be traceable to issues/PRs/releases rather than captured only in meetings.

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
Use short-lived branches from main. main must remain releasable/documentation-buildable. Long-lived feature branches are discouraged.

Suggested naming:

feature/<ticket>-short-name
fix/<ticket>-short-name
security/<ticket>-short-name
docs/<ticket>-short-name

docs.title: Pull request requirements
docs.text: Every PR contains: - problem/business context - implementation summary - affected modules - API/schema/migration impact - security impact - test evidence - rollback/compatibility notes where applicable - documentation/ADR updates

docs.title: Review rules
docs.text: At least one qualified reviewer for normal changes. Sensitive areas require an additional domain reviewer: - authentication/RBAC/signing/offline parser -> Security - entitlement/grant/policy -> Backend architecture/product owner - release/update/model OTA -> Release/Edge owner - DB migration -> Backend/data owner

docs.title: Merge policy
docs.text: Prefer squash or rebase according to repository setting, but final history must retain ticket/PR traceability. Direct commits to protected main should be disabled once team development begins.

docs.title: Commit content policy
docs.text: No secrets, private keys, customer exports, production credentials, decrypted model artifacts or proprietary binary releases should be committed to the documentation/source repository.

docs.title: Handbook Status & Ownership
docs.text: This handbook is the normative internal engineering baseline for LMS unless a newer approved ADR or product decision supersedes a section.

docs.title: Status taxonomy
docs.text:
• Approved — implementation baseline.
  • Proposed — recommended design awaiting approval.
  • Open Decision — implementation must preserve flexibility until resolved.
  • Deprecated — retained for historical reference only.
  • Phase 2 — deliberately deferred capability.

docs.text: Any code change that changes observable platform behavior, API contract, schema, release format, security boundary or operational procedure updates the handbook in the same PR.

docs.title: Approval rule
docs.text: Normal allocations within an approved entitlement may be single-admin or automated. Sensitive actions such as entitlement increase, large custom/perpetual grants, trial extension, forced LTS, major rehost, security/capacity override and signing-key changes use maker-checker approval.

docs.title: Release Approval SOP
docs.text: This SOP governs promotion into production-capable channels.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• Developer: produces Development/QA artifacts
  • QA: validates functional/integration/regression evidence
  • Security: validates security gates for applicable changes
  • Release Manager: owns promotion and rollout
  • Product/Architecture: approves material compatibility/policy impact when needed

docs.title: Promotion path
docs.text: Development -> QA -> Internal/Beta -> Stable -> LTS (explicit)

docs.title: Stable promotion evidence
docs.text: The promotion record references: - source commit/tag - build identity - signed release manifest - automated test report - upgrade/migration test - rollback test - compatibility matrix - capacity/benchmark impact if relevant - security scan/VAPT disposition - release notes - known issues and rollback trigger

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Stable promotion uses maker-checker: Release Manager requests; required QA/Security approver confirms evidence. Same actor must not self-approve when policy requires separation.

docs.title: LTS
docs.text: LTS is never automatic. Company explicitly designates an eligible Stable release as LTS after stability evidence and support-life decision.

docs.title: Emergency release
docs.text: Emergency releases may use an expedited path but still require source traceability, approval, signed artifacts, rollback plan and post-release review within the defined incident process.

docs.title: Requirements Coverage Audit
docs.text:

Audit result: the original handbook was strong but had several material omissions. The gaps listed under "Corrected in this audit" have now been added. Remaining items are intentional open decisions, not undocumented requirements.

docs.title: Remaining intentional open decisions
docs.text:
These are documented and should not be invented prematurely:

  1. Production human authentication / OIDC / SSO / MFA profile.
  2. Exact model content-key wrapping, secure local key storage and rotation profile.
  3. Final release archive/package format and script execution constraints.
  4. Telemetry privacy, opt-in/opt-out, retention and data residency.
  5. Enterprise HA topology and contractual RTO/RPO.
  6. Final API schemas/error catalog freeze after implementation review.
  7. Product-specific benchmark matrix and performance thresholds.
  8. Final support window for historical application versions.

docs.title: Audit conclusion
docs.text:
The handbook previously had real omissions in lifecycle state machines, required sequences, portal information architecture, trial eligibility, renewal milestones, device transfer/replacement, relay security, capacity authority, detailed inventory, artifact storage and several security threat details.

Those gaps are now explicitly documented.

Future handbook reviews should use this page as a regression checklist: if a design changes one of these requirements, the corresponding detailed page and this audit must be updated in the same PR.

docs.title: Engineering
docs.text:
• Typed Python where practical.
  • Pydantic at API boundaries.
  • Alembic only for production schema changes.
  • Structured logs with correlation IDs.
  • Explicit domain/service boundaries.
  • Authorization tests for tenant-scoped data.
  • Idempotency for retried workflows.
  • No secrets in source control.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Behaviour-changing PRs update the handbook.
  • Approved/proposed/open-decision status is explicit.
  • Mermaid is preferred for maintainable diagrams.
  • Material architecture changes require ADRs.
  • Real customer data is never used in examples.

docs.title: ERP Integration Contract
docs.text: ERP and LMS remain separate systems. Integration is intentionally narrow so the LMS does not become an accounting platform.

docs.title: Authority split
docs.text: Data System of record Invoice/payment state ERP Contract/order reference ERP Commercial SKU/order line ERP Customer operational device/site topology LMS Entitlement operational state LMS after approved import Allocation/grant state LMS Deployment/check-in state LMS

docs.title: Inbound ERP event example
docs.text:
{
  "event_id": "erp_evt_001",
  "event_type": "order_line_approved",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T10:00:00Z",
  "customer_external_ref": "CUST-1007",
  "contract_ref": "CTR-2031",
  "order_ref": "SO-9001",
  "line": {
    "product_code": "ANALYTICS_BASE",
    "feature_code": "PPE",
    "quantity": 40,
    "term": {"type": "subscription", "start": "2026-11-01", "end": "2027-10-31"}
  }
}

docs.title: Integration rules
docs.text:
• ERP events are idempotent by event_id.
  • Unknown product/SKU mapping is quarantined for review.
  • Payment/renewal status alone does not directly modify a device grant; LMS first updates entitlement state and then issues a new grant revision.
  • ERP retries are safe.
  • LMS never overwrites financial truth back into ERP unless a separate outbound contract explicitly permits it.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text: A scheduled reconciliation compares approved ERP commercial lines against LMS entitlements. Differences are categorized as missing, extra, quantity mismatch, term mismatch or mapping failure and surfaced to operations without destructive auto-correction.

docs.title: Licensing Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    E[Customer Entitlement Pool] --> A[Allocation]
    A --> G[Device-bound Signed Grant]
    G --> V[Local Verification]
    V --> R[Runtime Permission]

This separates commercial ownership from device execution.

docs.title: Transfer between customer/site ownership contexts
docs.text:
1. Create transfer request with current owner/site, requested owner/site, reason and effective intent.
  2. Validate caller authority and affected entitlements/allocations.
  3. Require approval according to policy; cross-customer transfer is always sensitive.
  4. Freeze or supersede grants that would become invalid under the new ownership.
  5. Update ownership/site assignments only after approval.
  6. Issue new grants under the valid target entitlement context.
  7. Reconcile old allocations and audit before/after ownership.

Silent overwrite of owner/site is prohibited.

docs.title: Replacement device
docs.text: For device replacement: - register replacement identity as a new device - approve replacement/rehost relationship - return or reassign allocation from retired device - issue new device-bound grant - retire old device/grant binding - preserve audit lineage between old and replacement devices

docs.title: Rehost
docs.text: Rehost is used when the physical system is intended to remain the same commercial installation but cryptographic/major hardware identity changed. Major motherboard/key changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED until approved.

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text:
Connected device: central revocation/superseding state is delivered at next sync/check-in according to policy.

Air-gapped device: immediate remote revocation is impossible. Revocation becomes effective after importing signed updated state or when current offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Diagnostics in grace/restricted state
docs.text: Where product safety permits, grace/restricted mode should preserve access to diagnostics, license recovery/import, support status and existing customer data. Expired commercial rights should disable unauthorized analytics execution, not make recovery impossible.

docs.title: Entitlements & Allocations
docs.text:
Example entitlement: PPE = 40 camera rights.

Device A = 16
Device B = 12
Device C = 8
Unallocated = 4

The customer/admin may redistribute rights without a new purchase while total allocation stays within the purchased pool.

docs.title: Reallocation controls
docs.text:
1. Validate total allocation.
  2. Calculate affected device grants.
  3. Issue superseding revisions.
  4. Prevent temporary double-allocation beyond approved transition policy.
  5. Synchronize online or through offline package.
  6. Audit before/after values and actor.

docs.title: Customer, device and site scope
docs.text:
A device is commercially owned by one customer but may serve multiple sites through explicit device-site assignments.

A device-bound grant may contain site-specific limits. Example:

{
  "device_id": "dev_x",
  "capability": "ppe_detection",
  "site_limits": [
    {"site_id": "site_a", "max_cameras": 4},
    {"site_id": "site_b", "max_cameras": 8}
  ]
}

The grant remains bound to the device, while constraints may partition the permitted quantity by site.

docs.title: Allocation invariant
docs.text:
For every entitlement item:

sum(active allocations) <= purchased/approved entitlement quantity

Reallocation must preserve this invariant transactionally and must not rely on UI-only validation.

docs.title: Signed Grant Canonical Format
docs.text: The signed grant is a device-verifiable authorization artifact. The final binary/serialization format is implementation-specific, but signing semantics must be deterministic.

docs.title: Canonical payload example
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "grant_id": "grant_001",
  "revision": 8,
  "supersedes": "grant_000",
  "issued_at": "2026-10-18T12:00:00Z",
  "subject": {
    "customer_id": "cust_001",
    "product_id": "analytics",
    "device_id": "dev_001"
  },
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "code": "ppe_detection",
      "limits": [{"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 4}],
      "dependencies": [{"capability": "analytics_base", "required": true}]
    }
  ],
  "commercial": {"type": "subscription", "valid_until": "2027-10-31T23:59:59Z"},
  "runtime": {"offline_days": 7, "grace_days": 7},
  "key_id": "lic_sign_01"
}

docs.title: Signing requirements
docs.text:
1. Remove the signature field from the payload.
  2. Normalize field order/encoding using a documented canonicalization method.
  3. Hash/sign the canonical bytes using the active license-signing key.
  4. Attach key_id, algorithm and signature.
  5. Device reconstructs the same canonical bytes before verification.

docs.title: Anti-rollback
docs.text: Device persists the highest accepted revision/sequence per relevant grant lineage and rejects older revisions unless an explicit signed recovery mechanism exists.

docs.title: Key rotation
docs.text: Verification trust store may contain current and retiring public keys. New grants use only the active key; older valid grants remain verifiable during the planned rotation window.

docs.title: Device-Bound Grants
docs.text:
A grant is the signed executable permission derived from entitlement, allocation and policy.

{
  "grant_id": "grant_1001",
  "device_id": "dev_310",
  "capabilities": [{
    "feature": "ppe_detection",
    "limit": {"type": "camera_count", "value": 4}
  }],
  "runtime_policy": {"offline_days": 7, "grace_days": 7},
  "revision": 2,
  "supersedes_grant_id": "grant_0988",
  "signature": "..."
}

Supersession is mandatory for replacement grants to prevent accidental aggregation.

Perpetual licenses may carry explicit update policies such as unlimited, N future major updates, or until-version.

docs.title: Dynamic License Policy Model
docs.text: The license system must avoid feature-specific columns such as ppe_enabled. Rights are represented by generic grants, constraints and dependencies.

docs.title: Grant model
docs.text: A grant contains: - subject scope: customer/product/device/site - capability code - grant type: base/add-on/trial/perpetual/subscription - quantity/limit constraints - valid-from / valid-until - offline/grace policy - revision and supersession - dependencies - update-right policy - signature metadata

docs.title: Constraint examples
docs.text:
[
  {"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 8},
  {"key": "site_id", "op": "in", "value": ["site_a", "site_b"]},
  {"key": "model_family", "op": "in", "value": ["ppe_v7"]}
]

docs.title: Update-right policy
docs.text:
Preferred explicit schema:

{
  "mode": "remaining_major_updates",
  "remaining_updates": 1,
  "until_version": null
}

Supported modes may include unlimited, during_active_term, remaining_major_updates, until_version, and none.

docs.title: Dependency semantics
docs.text: Dependent add-ons become dormant when required base grants are not active unless explicitly marked independent by policy.

docs.title: Renewal & Offline Validity
docs.text:
Three clocks remain independent:

  1. Commercial term/expiry.
  2. Offline authorization freshness — default 7 days unless overridden by policy.
  3. Grace/restriction period — default 7 days unless separately overridden.

A successful check-in never extends the paid commercial term.

A payment or central entitlement renewal does not activate an offline device until the new signed grant revision is delivered/imported and accepted locally.

docs.title: Reminder baseline
docs.text:
Default proposed reminders are 30 days, 7 days and 1 day before expiry, configurable by product/customer policy.

flowchart LR
    A[Due Soon / Reminder] --> B[Renewal Requested]
    B --> C[Commercial Approval]
    C --> D[Entitlement Term Updated]
    D --> E[New Signed Grant Revision]
    E --> F{Delivery}
    F -->|Online| G[Delivered]
    F -->|Offline| H[Export / Import]
    G --> I[Local Verify]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Atomic Accept / Active]
    J --> K[Receipt / Reconciliation]

docs.title: Status milestones
docs.text:
• Due Soon
  • Requested
  • Approved / Grant Issued
  • Delivered / Imported
  • Accepted / Active
  • Failed / Rejected
  • Expired / Restricted

Issued != Delivered != Accepted.

If delivery or verification fails, the old grant continues according to its own expiry/grace rules. Where product safety permits, restricted/grace mode should preserve diagnostics, license recovery/import and access to existing customer data while unauthorized analytics execution is disabled.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
• Default trial period is 7 days.
  • Duration is policy/campaign configurable by feature, product or approved customer exception.
  • Trial starts at first successful feature activation, not request, issuance, package download or import.
  • Trial is a signed time-limited device-bound grant, not a UI flag.
  • Baseline eligibility is one trial per customer entitlement + feature.
  • Admin/campaign override may permit extension or an additional trial, but the override is auditable and may require maker-checker approval.
  • Globally reusable trial licenses are prohibited.

docs.title: Add-ons
docs.text:
Subscription add-ons normally co-terminate with the active base subscription.

Base: Jan 1 ---------------- Dec 31
PPE:                 Sep 1 -- Dec 31
Renewal: Jan 1 ---- Base + PPE together

Commercial pricing may be prorated for the remaining base term. An explicitly independent add-on may carry its own term when product/commercial policy permits it.

Perpetual base licenses may have subscription add-ons.

Dependent add-ons become dormant when their required base is inactive unless the add-on policy explicitly marks them independent.

docs.title: Purchase/activation distinction
docs.text: A trial request, purchase request, payment approval or marketplace selection does not itself authorize runtime execution. The device still requires a valid signed grant and all compatibility/capacity/install/health gates.

docs.title: Marketplace & OTA
docs.text:
Marketplace and OTA are separate capabilities in one LMS.

  • Marketplace: what can this customer/device discover, trial or buy?
  • OTA: how are compatible application/model components safely delivered, installed and rolled back?

They reuse the same customer, device, entitlement, capacity and audit data.

docs.title: Deployment Job State Machine
docs.text: Deployment orchestration must be restart-safe and deterministic.

docs.title: Job states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> Scheduled
    Scheduled --> Running
    Running --> Completed
    Running --> PartiallyFailed
    Running --> Failed
    Scheduled --> Cancelled
    Running --> Cancelling
    Cancelling --> Cancelled

docs.title: Target states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pending
    Pending --> WaitingWindow
    WaitingWindow --> Preflight
    Preflight --> Downloading
    Downloading --> Verifying
    Verifying --> Staging
    Staging --> Installing
    Installing --> HealthCheck
    HealthCheck --> Active
    HealthCheck --> RollingBack
    RollingBack --> RolledBack
    Preflight --> Blocked
    Verifying --> Failed
    Installing --> Failed

docs.title: Retry policy
docs.text:
• Network/artifact transient failures may retry with exponential backoff.
  • Signature/hash/compatibility failures are non-retryable until input changes.
  • Installation failure triggers rollback before retry consideration.
  • Automatic mode obeys maintenance window and concurrency limits.
  • Manual mode requires explicit deployment approval/start.

docs.title: Completion semantics
docs.text: A job is Completed only when every target reaches Active or an explicitly accepted terminal exclusion state. PartiallyFailed preserves successful targets and clearly reports failed/rolled-back targets.

docs.title: Deployment & Rollback
docs.text:
Policy hierarchy:

Platform Default -> Customer Policy -> Site Policy -> Device Override

Supported settings include AUTO/MANUAL, channel, maintenance window, model-only OTA, application OTA, concurrency and auto-rollback.

Default automatic maintenance window: 01:00–03:00, customer configurable.

Rollback restores a coherent release set, not only one binary. Keep 2–3 known-good releases when disk permits; always preserve at least the immediately previous known-good version.

docs.title: Model Manifest Schema
docs.text: Model metadata is independent from application releases so compatible model-only OTA does not force application redownload.

docs.title: Example

  "manifest_version": 1,
  "model_release_id": "mr_ppe_7_3_0",
  "model_id": "ppe_detector",
  "version": "7.3.0",
  "channel": "stable",
  "framework": "TensorRT",
  "precision": "FP16",
  "input": {"width": 640, "height": 640},
  "compatibility": {
    "architectures": ["x86_64"],
    "gpu_families": ["nvidia"],
    "runtime": ">=3.7 <4.0",
    "feature_release": ">=4.2 <5.0"
  },
  "artifact": {
    "uri_ref": "artifact://models/ppe/7.3.0",
    "sha256": "...",
    "encrypted": true,

}

docs.title: Key handling principle
docs.text: The repository stores encrypted model material. Entitlement controls permission to use the model; device authorization controls decryption. A universal embedded model password is prohibited.

docs.title: Model OTA
docs.text:
AI models are first-class managed artifacts with identity, semantic version, framework/runtime, hardware compatibility, precision, encrypted hash, size, release channel and feature compatibility.

flowchart TD
    A[Publish Model Release] --> B[Validate Metadata]
    B --> C[Encrypt Artifact]
    C --> D[Sign Artifact / Manifest]
    D --> E[Assign Channel]
    E --> F[Resolve Target Devices]
    F --> G[Compatibility + Capacity Check]
    G --> H[Download / Import]
    H --> I[Verify Signature + Hash]
    I --> J[Authorize Decryption]
    J --> K[Stage Model]
    K --> L[Warm-up / Health Check]
    L -->|Pass| M[Activate]
    L -->|Fail| N[Rollback]

If a required model already exists locally, it must not be downloaded again.

docs.title: Release Manifest Schema
docs.text: The release manifest is the machine-readable contract between Release Management and the edge Update Manager. It is signed and immutable after publication.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
