  "manifest_version": 1,
  "release_id": "rel_ppe_4_2_1",
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "version": "4.2.1",
  "channel": "stable",
  "platforms": [
    {"os": "ubuntu", "versions": ["22.04", "24.04"], "arch": ["x86_64", "aarch64"]}
  ],
  "requirements": {
    "runtime": ">=3.7 <4.0",
    "disk_free_mb": 2500,
    "ram_mb": 8192
  },
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "artifact_id": "art_app_421",
      "type": "application",
      "version": "4.2.1",
      "sha256": "...",
      "size": 123456789
    }
  ],
  "models": [
    {"model_id": "ppe_detector", "version_range": ">=7.3 <8.0", "required": true}
  ],
  "migrations": {
    "config_schema_from": [4,5],
    "config_schema_to": 6,
    "automatic": true
  },
  "health_checks": [
    {"type": "http", "target": "http://127.0.0.1:9000/health", "timeout_sec": 30}
  ],
  "rollback": {"supported": true, "minimum_free_mb": 3000},
  "signature": {"key_id": "release_sign_01", "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "..."}
}

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Manifest canonicalization is defined before signing.
  • Artifact hash is mandatory.
  • Dependencies use explicit version ranges.
  • Installation scripts are treated as signed artifacts, never unsigned inline commands.
  • A published manifest is immutable; corrections create a new release/version.
  • Device must reject unsupported manifest versions.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Development -> QA -> Beta/Internal -> Stable -> LTS -> Retired

Automatic production updates consume Stable by default. LTS targeting is explicitly controlled by the company.

docs.title: Traditional package standard
docs.text:
release/
├── manifest.json
├── application/
├── ui/
├── migrations/
├── configs/
├── dependencies/
├── install/
│   ├── install.sh
│   ├── rollback.sh
│   └── healthcheck.sh
└── signature

No manual site migration should be required in normal releases.

docs.title: Semantic versioning intent
docs.text: Application, feature/plugin and model versions should use a predictable version scheme. Semantic versioning is recommended for software interfaces where practical.

docs.title: Compatibility declarations
docs.text: Every release declares supported: - OS/version and architecture - application/runtime ranges - dependent feature/plugin ranges - model ranges - configuration schema versions - minimum hardware/runtime requirements

docs.title: Support window
docs.text: The organization must define how many previous application versions remain upgrade-supported. Until finalized, release manifests must explicitly declare supported source versions rather than assuming any historical version can upgrade directly.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text: Breaking local API, manifest or grant-format changes require: 1. schema/version bump 2. compatibility/migration plan 3. dual-read or staged migration when necessary 4. explicit support-window communication 5. rollback testing

docs.title: Model compatibility
docs.text: Model releases are independently versioned but must declare compatible feature/runtime ranges. A model-only update is allowed only when those constraints pass.

docs.title: Backup & Recovery
docs.text:
Back up PostgreSQL state, audit data, artifact metadata, release manifests, artifact repository and reconstruction configuration.

Signing private keys use a separate protected backup/recovery process and are never handled as normal database backup material.

Phase 1 SaaS baseline: single primary + automated backups + monitoring + documented recovery, while remaining HA-ready.

docs.title: Backup classes
docs.text:
• transactional PostgreSQL backups
  • artifact repository backups/replication
  • audit data backups
  • configuration/reconstruction metadata
  • signing-key recovery through its separate protected mechanism

docs.title: Proposed retention baseline
docs.text: Retention must be finalized by operations/compliance, but the implementation should support daily/weekly/monthly policy tiers and customer-specific extensions.

docs.title: Restore validation
docs.text: A backup is not considered reliable until restore is tested. Scheduled restore exercises verify: - DB integrity and migration compatibility - artifact hashes - audit availability - application startup - customer/tenant access behavior - signing integration restoration without exposing key material

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Restore exercises record backup ID, environment, restore duration, validation checks, failures/exceptions and remediation owner.

docs.title: Customer-Hosted Deployment Topology
docs.text: Customer-hosted LMS uses the same application codebase with deployment-mode configuration.

docs.title: Baseline topology
docs.text:
flowchart TB

    RP --> LMS[LMS Application]
    LMS --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]

docs.title: Minimum production requirements
docs.text:
• TLS termination
  • persistent PostgreSQL storage
  • persistent artifact storage
  • backup destination
  • secrets/configuration outside source code
  • monitoring/log export
  • time synchronization
  • outbound email if notifications are enabled

docs.title: Upgrade model
docs.text: Customer-hosted LMS self-update is manual in the initial product. Vendor supplies a signed LMS release package/runbook; customer/operator executes upgrade within an approved maintenance window.

docs.title: HA
docs.text: HA is an enterprise option rather than mandatory Phase 1 baseline. Exact topology and RTO/RPO are decided per deployment tier.

docs.title: Disaster Recovery & Continuity
docs.text: Phase 1 remains operationally simple but recovery is designed before production.

docs.title: Proposed recovery tiers
docs.text: Component Baseline approach PostgreSQL automated encrypted backups + tested restore Artifact repository versioned/replicated object storage or protected backup Audit data protected backup; append-only semantics Signing metadata database backup; private keys handled separately Signing keys KMS/HSM/provider-specific protected recovery Customer-hosted LMS documented manual restore package/process

docs.title: RTO/RPO
docs.text: Exact enterprise RTO/RPO remain an open business/operations decision. Until approved, no team should promise contractual recovery targets.

docs.title: Mandatory DR testing
docs.text:
• scheduled restore test
  • database migration + restore compatibility test
  • artifact integrity verification
  • signing-key recovery procedure exercise without exposing key material
  • documentation of measured restore time and exceptions

docs.title: Environment classes
docs.text: Environment Purpose Data rule Release channels Local Dev developer iteration synthetic only Development Integration service/edge integration synthetic/test Development/QA QA formal validation synthetic/anonymized QA/Internal Staging production-like readiness anonymized/approved Internal/Stable candidate Production customer service real customer data Stable/LTS only

docs.title: Separation requirements
docs.text:
• Separate credentials and secrets per environment.
  • Production signing keys are never available in lower environments.
  • Development/QA artifacts cannot be promoted implicitly into production; promotion creates explicit approved release state.
  • Test tenants/devices are clearly marked.
  • Production backups are not restored into lower environments without approved sanitization.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is supplied through environment/secret manager/deployment configuration, never hard-coded. Environment-specific settings include DB connection, artifact storage, signing provider, email provider, telemetry endpoints and auth mode.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: All servers use reliable time synchronization. Persist timestamps in UTC. Site timezone is used for display and maintenance-window interpretation.

docs.title: Incident Response
docs.text: Incident response covers security events and operational failures that materially affect licensing, deployment, model protection or customer availability.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Detect -> Triage -> Contain -> Recover -> Validate -> Communicate -> Post-incident review

docs.title: Immediate evidence
docs.text: Preserve: - request/correlation IDs - audit events - deployment job/target history - relevant application/security logs - artifact/release hashes - grant revisions - signing key IDs (never private key material) - timestamps and operator actions

docs.title: Suspected signing-key compromise
docs.text:
1. stop new signing using affected key
  2. activate approved replacement key if available
  3. identify artifacts/grants signed by impacted key
  4. assess online/offline blast radius
  5. distribute trust/key-rotation update using approved path
  6. revoke/supersede affected grants/artifacts where required
  7. initiate security incident and post-incident review

docs.title: Widespread bad release
docs.text:
1. stop rollout/concurrency queue
  2. mark release blocked
  3. trigger rollback to known-good release set
  4. verify health receipts
  5. preserve failed installation evidence
  6. communicate affected customers

docs.title: Tenant-isolation suspicion
docs.text: Treat as security-critical until disproven. Freeze risky admin actions, preserve evidence, scope affected data and escalate immediately.

docs.title: Communications
docs.text: External communications contain confirmed impact and recovery guidance only. Technical hypotheses and sensitive security details remain internal until validated.

docs.title: Monitoring & ERP Integration
docs.text:
Monitor API availability/latency, DB health, signing errors, grant issuance failures, deployment/rollback failures, stale check-ins, rollout progress, capacity failures, artifact errors and notification failures.

ERP remains separate and may be authoritative for orders, invoices/payment and contracts. LMS remains authoritative for operational entitlement, allocations, device grants, activation, trials, deployment and local acceptance.

docs.title: Notification Events & Templates
docs.text: Phase 1 channels are portal + email. The event model must allow webhooks later without changing business modules.

docs.title: Notification event catalogue
docs.text: Event Default audience Urgency renewal_due_30d Customer Admin, Vendor account owner normal renewal_due_7d Customer Admin, Vendor account owner high renewal_due_1d Customer Admin, Vendor account owner high license_entered_grace Customer Admin, Support high offline_checkin_stale Customer Admin, Support high trial_expiring Customer Admin normal trial_expired Customer Admin normal deployment_scheduled Customer/Site Admin normal deployment_failed Customer/Site Admin, Support high rollback_completed Support, Release Manager high device_rehost_required Customer Admin, Support high entitlement_overallocation_attempt Customer Admin, Support normal

docs.title: Template rules
docs.text: Templates include customer/site/device display names, safe remediation steps and portal deep-link identifiers. They never include secrets, raw license payloads, private keys or decrypted model information.

docs.title: Delivery tracking
docs.text: Persist notification ID, event ID, recipient, channel, template version, send attempt, result and delivered timestamp. Repeated transient failures retry with backoff; permanent failures are visible to operations.

docs.title: Operational Runbook Baseline
docs.text: Runbooks must be executable by support/operations without requiring source-code knowledge.

docs.title: Required runbooks before production
docs.text:
1. LMS API unavailable
  2. PostgreSQL degraded/unavailable
  3. Signing service unavailable
  4. Artifact repository unavailable
  5. Failed Stable rollout
  6. Mass rollback
  7. Offline bundle rejected at customer site
  8. Device stuck in REHOST_REQUIRED
  9. Customer over-allocation conflict
  10. Suspected signing-key compromise
  11. Backup restore
  12. ERP synchronization mismatch

docs.title: Runbook format
docs.text: Each runbook contains: - symptoms and alerts - customer impact - safety checks - diagnostic steps - approved remediation - rollback/recovery - escalation owner - audit/evidence to retain - post-incident follow-up

docs.title: Incident severity proposal
docs.text: Severity Description Example Sev-1 broad critical outage/security compromise signing-key compromise, platform-wide license failure Sev-2 major customer/service impairment deployment/renewal failure affecting many devices Sev-3 limited degradation single-customer update issue with workaround Sev-4 minor/non-urgent cosmetic portal issue

docs.title: L1 — Operations / Support
docs.text: Handles known runbooks, customer/site/device lookup, entitlement/grant status checks, offline package validation and standard rehost/renewal coordination.

docs.title: L2 — Engineering
docs.text: Engaged for reproducible product defects, migration/update failures, capacity anomalies, integration issues and unsupported states not resolved by runbook.

docs.title: L3 — Architecture / Security / Release
docs.text: Engaged for signing/key incidents, tenant isolation, systemic release failures, data integrity risk, cross-module design defects and emergency architecture decisions.

docs.title: Escalation packet
docs.text:
Every escalation includes: - customer/site/device IDs - request/correlation ID - error code - timestamps/timezone - current grant/release/model revisions - deployment/installation receipt state - relevant safe logs - steps already attempted - business/customer impact

Avoid sending secrets or decrypted model material through ordinary support channels.

docs.title: Device cannot activate feature
docs.text:
1. Identify customer/site/device and request ID.
  2. Check registration state and device ownership.
  3. Check entitlement and allocation.
  4. Check latest grant issuance/delivery/acceptance state.
  5. Check commercial expiry, offline freshness and grace separately.
  6. Check device-reported rejection code.
  7. Check capacity/compatibility and installed release/model dependencies.
  8. If offline, validate request/response pairing and nonce.
  9. Apply only approved remediation; do not hand-edit grants.
  10. Record resolution/audit reference.

docs.title: Offline package rejected
docs.text:
1. Confirm package was created for the same device/request ID.
  2. Verify operator did not reuse an older response.
  3. Compare device accepted revision vs response revision.
  4. Check signature/key trust status.
  5. Check release/model compatibility.
  6. Export a fresh request if nonce/request expired or state changed.

docs.title: Deployment failed and rolled back
docs.text:
1. Confirm rollback health status.
  2. Capture installation receipt and request ID.
  3. Identify failed stage: download, verify, stage, migration, start, health check.
  4. Check disk/dependency/runtime prerequisites.
  5. Block release for broader rollout if systemic.
  6. Escalate to Release Manager when failure rate crosses rollout threshold.

docs.title: Rehost required
docs.text:
1. Confirm major hardware/key identity change.
  2. Verify customer/device ownership.
  3. Collect previous/new fingerprint evidence.
  4. Submit rehost request and required approval.
  5. Rebind identity and issue superseding grant.
  6. Retire old binding and return/reconcile allocation.

docs.title: Renewal approved but device still expired
docs.text:
1. Confirm ERP/commercial approval reached LMS.
  2. Confirm new entitlement term and grant revision exist.
  3. Check whether device has delivered/imported the new revision.
  4. For offline site, produce/import renewed response package.
  5. Confirm device accepted revision and generated receipt.

docs.title: Signing service unavailable
docs.text:
1. Stop repeated manual issuance attempts.
  2. Confirm signing gateway/provider health.
  3. Existing valid grants continue according to policy; do not bypass signature requirement.
  4. Queue issuance via outbox/retry.
  5. Escalate according to incident severity if customer activations/renewals are blocked.

docs.title: Product & Scope
docs.text: The LMS is a reusable enterprise control plane for current and future AI products. It centralizes customer/site/device management, licensing, entitlement pools, Marketplace/OTA, model lifecycle, capacity planning, renewal, audit and offline operations.

docs.title: Primary actors
docs.text:
• Vendor Super Admin
  • Product Admin
  • Release Manager
  • Security Approver
  • Developer
  • Support Engineer
  • Customer Admin
  • Site Admin
  • Read-Only Auditor
  • Edge Device / Server

A device belongs commercially to a customer but may serve one or more sites.

docs.title: Consolidated Business Rules
docs.text: This page is the normative cross-domain business-rule checklist for LMS. More detailed pages remain authoritative for implementation specifics.

docs.title: Licensing and entitlement
docs.text:
• Registration, commercial licensing and capacity validation are separate states.
  • Entitlement = what the customer owns; allocation = distribution of pooled rights; grant = device-bound signed executable authorization.
  • Customer pooled quantity must never be over-allocated.
  • Reallocation creates superseding grants and must not allow old/new quantities to remain simultaneously usable indefinitely.
  • Subscription and perpetual base licenses are supported.
  • Subscription add-ons co-terminate with the base by default; explicitly independent add-ons may have their own term.
  • A perpetual base may carry subscription add-ons.
  • Dependent add-ons become dormant when the required base is inactive.
  • Commercial expiry, offline authorization freshness and grace are three independent clocks.
  • Successful check-in never extends commercial expiry.
  • Payment/renewal approval alone does not renew an offline device until it receives and accepts the new signed grant revision.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
• Default trial duration is 7 days and is policy-configurable.
  • Trial starts on first successful feature activation, not on request, issuance or package import.
  • Baseline eligibility is one trial per customer entitlement + feature, unless an auditable admin/campaign override permits another trial.
  • A trial is a signed time-limited grant; globally reusable trial licenses are prohibited.

docs.title: Device lifecycle
docs.text:
• Device identity is cryptographic key + versioned weighted hardware fingerprint; MAC is evidence only.
  • Minor hardware changes trigger re-evaluation and normally continue.
  • Major identity changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED; they do not silently destroy or transfer licenses.
  • Decommission/replacement returns eligible allocation to the entitlement pool after approval/reconciliation.
  • Device transfer is request/approval/audit driven; ownership is never silently overwritten.
  • Air-gapped revocation becomes effective only after signed state is imported or existing offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Capacity
docs.text:
• Central capacity assessment is advisory/pre-assessment; local capacity check is authoritative for actual activation.
  • Commercial rights are never silently reduced because hardware is insufficient.
  • Capacity engine recommends alternatives; an operator/customer chooses the allowed configuration.

docs.title: Marketplace and OTA
docs.text:
• Marketplace discovery/trial/purchase does not itself authorize execution.
  • A feature activates only when compatible, licensed, installed, healthy and capacity-validated.
  • Automatic production updates consume Stable by default.
  • LTS deployment is explicitly company-controlled.
  • Normal site releases must automate migration, health-check and rollback; no manual migration step.
  • Models are independently versioned, encrypted, signed and inventory-aware.
  • Offline bundles should contain only missing/required artifacts where possible.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
• High-risk actions use maker-checker approval.
  • Audit retention baseline is configurable 1–3 years.
  • Portal + email are initial notification channels; webhook delivery remains extensible.
  • LMS is not an accounting system; ERP integration is separate.

docs.title: Approved Decisions
docs.text: Decision Baseline Backend Python 3.12 + FastAPI modular monolith Database PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy + Alembic Admin UI React + Vite + TypeScript Deployment SaaS and customer-hosted OS Ubuntu/Linux first; future Windows-compatible abstractions Development auth Username/password; production IAM later ADR Trial Default 7 days, configurable; starts at first successful feature activation Offline validity Default 7 days, hierarchical override Grace Default 7 days, independently configurable Add-ons Normally co-terminate with subscription base Capacity Recommend; never silently alter purchased rights Packaging Traditional signed release bundles; no Docker dependency Auto OTA Supported; Stable channel by default Maintenance window Default 01:00–03:00; customer configurable Rollback Keep 2–3 known-good versions where disk permits Model OTA Independent, encrypted, signed and rollback-capable Audit retention Configurable; baseline 1–3 years ERP Separate system with synchronization interfaces

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. One common licensing platform for multiple product families.
  2. Same codebase for SaaS and customer-hosted deployment.
  3. Connected, intermittently connected and fully air-gapped operation.
  4. Highly customized licensing without hard-coded feature columns.
  5. Entitlement pooling with device-specific allocations and grants.
  6. Hardware capability and combined-workload validation before activation.
  7. Trial, purchase, add-on and renewal flows in one platform.
  8. Traditional package OTA plus independent encrypted model OTA.
  9. Automatic/manual update policies, maintenance windows and rollback.
  10. Corporate-grade audit, approval and security controls.

docs.title: Phase 1 non-goals
docs.text:
• Full ERP/accounting capability.
  • Windows-first implementation.
  • Automatic customer-hosted LMS self-upgrade.
  • Premature microservice decomposition.
  • Claiming complete tamper resistance on a root-compromised edge host.

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Term Meaning Entitlement Central commercial right purchased or granted to a customer. Entitlement Pool Quantity/rights available to a customer for allocation. Allocation Distribution of pooled rights to devices/sites. Grant Signed, device-bound executable permission derived from entitlement and policy. Trial Grant Time-limited signed grant; default 7 days unless overridden. Offline Validity Time a device may continue without authorized sync/check-in. Grace Restricted period after commercial expiry or policy condition. Release Versioned application/feature/UI/runtime package metadata. Model Release Independently versioned encrypted AI model artifact. Release Set Coherent application, feature, UI, runtime and model snapshot for deployment/rollback. Capacity Assessment Combined workload feasibility evaluation using inventory and benchmark evidence.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria by Delivery Phase
docs.text: These are minimum exit criteria for phase completion; detailed stories may add stricter criteria.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Trust foundation
docs.text:
• device generates/loads protected key pair
  • enrollment rejects invalid/reused authorization
  • signed grant verifies offline
  • wrong-device/tampered/expired/stale-revision grants are rejected
  • last-known-time rollback scenario is covered by tests
  • audit events exist for enrollment and issuance

docs.title: Phase 2 — Registry & licensing
docs.text:
• customer/site/device topology supports multi-site server assignment
  • entitlement pool cannot be over-allocated
  • reallocations supersede affected device grants
  • base/add-on dependency works
  • subscription and perpetual terms represented without schema change
  • decommission returns rights to pool

docs.title: Phase 3 — Capacity
docs.text:
• stable inventory separated from resource snapshots
  • benchmark profile/version recorded in assessment
  • combined existing+proposed workload evaluated
  • warning/fail produces recommendations
  • commercial quantity remains unchanged on capacity failure

docs.title: Phase 4 — Marketplace & release management
docs.text:
• marketplace hides/disables ineligible actions with reason
  • trial duration can be configured
  • trial starts only after successful activation
  • Stable/LTS channel rules enforced
  • release manifest is immutable and signed
  • unsupported dependency/OS/runtime is blocked

docs.title: Phase 5 — Model OTA & deployment
docs.text:
• installed model inventory prevents unnecessary redownload
  • encrypted model cannot be used without authorization
  • model-only OTA supported
  • automatic/manual modes supported
  • default maintenance window 01:00–03:00 and override works
  • failed health check restores previous coherent release set

docs.title: Phase 6 — Lifecycle
docs.text:
• commercial expiry, offline validity and grace behave independently
  • check-in does not extend commercial term
  • offline renewal can be imported and reconciled
  • revocation behavior is correct for online and air-gapped cases
  • major identity change triggers rehost flow

docs.title: Phase 7 — Hardening
docs.text:
• backup restore successfully rehearsed
  • VAPT findings triaged/remediated per release policy
  • tenant-isolation tests pass
  • monitoring/alerts cover critical workflows
  • operational and support runbooks reviewed
  • production readiness checklist signed off

docs.title: Minimum automation expectation
docs.text: Critical-path API and edge verification tests run in CI. Upgrade/rollback, offline bundle, migration and hardware-capacity scenarios run in dedicated integration/system environments with representative fixtures.

docs.title: Definition of Ready / Definition of Done
Definition of Ready
docs.text: A story/epic is Ready when: - business outcome and acceptance criteria are written - affected actors/scopes are known - state transition is defined - API/data ownership is identified - authorization and tenant boundary are defined - online/offline behaviour is explicit - error/recovery path is documented - security/capacity impact is classified - dependencies and migration needs are known - test approach is identified

docs.title: Definition of Done
docs.text: A change is Done when: - implementation is merged through review - unit/integration/contract tests pass - tenant authorization tests exist where applicable - audit and observability are implemented - DB/API compatibility and migration are validated - upgrade and rollback are tested where applicable - threat/security review is complete - documentation and ADRs are updated in the same PR - acceptance criteria are demonstrated - no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 defects remain for release scope

docs.title: Release Readiness
docs.text:
• Requirements accepted
  • ADR impact reviewed
  • Code review complete
  • Unit/integration tests green
  • DB migration tested
  • Upgrade from supported prior release tested
  • Rollback tested
  • Package/model signatures validated
  • Capacity metadata reviewed
  • Security scans complete
  • VAPT requirements satisfied
  • Release notes complete
  • Stable/LTS approval recorded

docs.title: Test Strategy
docs.text: Required layers: unit, database/repository, API integration, tenant-isolation, central-edge contract, signature tamper, offline request/response, rehost, capacity regression, install/upgrade, migration, rollback, model-only OTA, interruption recovery and security/VAPT.

docs.title: Security Architecture
docs.text: Goals: prevent unauthorized grant issuance, detect tampering, bind grants to device identity, limit replay/rollback, isolate tenants, protect model IP, maintain auditable admin history and retain recovery capability without exposing signing keys.

docs.title: Security & Privileged Action Matrix
docs.text:
Action Minimum role Second approval Audit View customer/device state Support / Customer Admin scoped No Access log Allocate within entitlement pool Customer/Vendor Admin scoped Normally no Yes Increase entitlement Commercial/Product Admin Yes unless ERP-approved automation Yes Issue exceptional perpetual/custom grant Product Admin Yes Yes Rehost after motherboard/device-key change Support/Admin Yes Yes Publish Development/QA release Developer/Release Manager No Yes Promote Stable/LTS Release Manager Yes, QA/Security gate Yes Override capacity/security block Privileged Admin Yes Yes Rotate signing key Security/DevOps Yes Yes Revoke grant/device Admin/Support policy High-impact cases yes Yes

Development roles may create/test plugins and artifacts only in non-production channels unless separately authorized.

docs.title: Assisted-Offline Relay Security
docs.text: The relay workstation/laptop is a transport convenience, never a licensing authority.

docs.title: Required properties
docs.text:
• no license or release signing private keys
  • short-lived/operator-scoped authentication to the central LMS where connectivity exists
  • encrypted local storage for staged request/response packages where feasible
  • automatic cleanup/retention policy for staged packages
  • no universal customer/device secrets
  • package integrity preserved end-to-end; relay cannot modify signed content undetected
  • audit of upload/download operator and request ID where possible

docs.title: Lost or compromised relay
docs.text: Compromise of the relay should expose at most staged encrypted/signed package material and short-lived credentials, not signing authority. Replayed/stolen response packages remain bound to request ID, nonce and device identity.

docs.title: Secure Coding Standard
docs.text: This standard applies to backend, portal, edge agents, update tooling and offline package parsers.

docs.title: Input and parser safety
docs.text:
• Treat all external input as untrusted.
  • Validate types, ranges, lengths and enum values.
  • Reject unknown critical fields in signed/canonical payloads where ambiguity would be dangerous.
  • Bound archive extraction size/file count.
  • Prevent path traversal and symlink escape.
  • Never execute unsigned scripts or packages.

docs.title: Authentication and authorization
docs.text:
• Authenticate before authorization.
  • Enforce permission + scope at service/use-case boundaries.
  • Never trust customer/site/device IDs supplied by clients without scope validation.
  • No authorization logic only in UI.

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
• Use approved libraries; do not implement custom primitives.
  • Never log secret/private key material.
  • Separate key purposes.
  • Make signature verification fail closed.
  • Verify signature before processing executable/decryptable artifact content wherever practical.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• Parameterized ORM/query usage only.
  • Explicit transaction boundaries.
  • Tenant/customer predicates in business queries.
  • Migrations reviewed for destructive/locking impact.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Log request ID, actor/object IDs and safe diagnostic context. Do not log passwords, tokens, private keys, raw license secrets, decrypted models or customer-sensitive payloads.

docs.title: Dependency security
docs.text: Pin/constraint dependencies, scan for known vulnerabilities and maintain a documented upgrade/remediation process.

docs.title: Security Control Baseline
docs.text: This is the minimum security baseline for development and release readiness. It does not replace customer-specific compliance requirements.

docs.title: Identity and access
docs.text:
• deny-by-default RBAC
  • password hashing using an approved adaptive password hash in development auth
  • privileged role changes audited
  • no shared administrator accounts
  • session/token expiry and revocation
  • future production IAM adapter without rewriting authorization model

docs.title: Application security
docs.text:
• input validation at all API/file-import boundaries
  • allowlisted parsers and bounded archive extraction
  • protection against path traversal and archive bombs
  • CSRF protection where cookie sessions are used
  • CORS restricted by deployment policy
  • rate limiting for login/enrollment/import abuse surfaces
  • secure headers for portal
  • dependency/SCA and SAST in CI

docs.title: Data security
docs.text:
• TLS for central network transport
  • secrets outside source control
  • database least-privilege credentials
  • encrypted backups
  • artifact integrity by hash and signature
  • model artifacts encrypted in storage/distribution
  • no raw passwords/private keys/decrypted models in logs

docs.title: Signing boundary
docs.text:
• separate license-signing and release-signing key purpose
  • key ID/version recorded in artifacts
  • rotation supported without breaking old verification immediately
  • signing request authorization and audit
  • production custody via KMS/HSM/equivalent protected service where feasible

docs.title: Offline import security
docs.text:
• signed/canonical request payload
  • nonce/request ID and expiry
  • device binding
  • anti-replay storage
  • strict package size/content validation
  • signatures checked before execution/decryption

docs.title: Secure SDLC gates
docs.text: Threat review -> code review -> automated security scan -> QA -> VAPT as required -> remediation -> release approval.

docs.title: Signing & Model Protection
docs.text:
• Grants are digitally signed.
  • Software/model manifests and artifacts are separately signed.
  • License-signing and release-signing use separate key purposes.
  • Private signing keys stay outside normal application storage.
  • Devices verify using trusted public keys.
  • Production should use managed KMS/HSM-backed custody or equivalent protected boundary where feasible.

Model baseline: entitlement-controlled, device-authorized decryption. Avoid one universal model password. Exact key wrapping and secure local key storage remain a Security ADR.

docs.title: Tenant Isolation Standard
docs.text: SaaS mode is multi-tenant. Cross-tenant disclosure or mutation is treated as a security-critical defect.

docs.title: Enforcement model
docs.text: Every business object is associated with a customer/tenant directly or through a verified ownership path. Authorization resolves caller scope before repository/service operations.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Never accept customer_id as proof of access.
  • Repository methods for tenant data require explicit scope/context.
  • Background jobs carry tenant identity with the job payload.
  • Audit queries are tenant-scoped unless caller has explicit global audit permission.
  • Artifact/deployment targets are validated against customer ownership before delivery.
  • Customer-hosted mode may be single-customer, but code paths remain compatible with tenant checks.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
1. user from Customer A cannot read Customer B object by ID
  2. user from A cannot enumerate B through filters/search
  3. user from A cannot mutate B using guessed IDs
  4. background jobs cannot cross tenant due to missing scope
  5. offline request for one customer cannot obtain another customer's grant/artifact
  6. support/global roles are tested for both allowed and denied scope combinations

Tenant isolation regression tests are release blockers.

docs.title: Threat Model & VAPT
docs.text: Threat Baseline control Enrollment/token guessing High entropy, short-lived/single-use authorization, rate limiting Forged license Protected central signing key + digitally signed grants Tampered package/model Signature + hash + manifest verification MAC spoofing Device cryptographic key + weighted/versioned fingerprint; MAC only evidence Device cloning Device-bound grants, protected local key/state, quantity controls Clock rollback Persist last-known trusted time; suspicious backward jumps cause reject/restrict until revalidation Grant rollback Monotonic revision/sequence and protected local accepted-state Request replay Nonce, request hash, expiry, idempotency, device binding Stolen/compromised relay Transport-only role, short-lived auth, encrypted staging where feasible, no signing authority Tenant escape Strict tenant-scoped authorization and negative isolation tests Update crash Atomic staging, health check, coherent release-set rollback Transfer/rehost abuse Approval, maker-checker for sensitive cases, immutable audit lineage Signing-key compromise Key-purpose separation, rotation/recovery plan, incident procedure Offline revocation delay Accepted design limitation; revoke on signed import or offline expiry Fully compromised/root edge Software signatures/hardening reduce risk but cannot guarantee tamper-proof execution on a hostile root-controlled host

docs.title: VAPT coverage
docs.text:
VAPT/release security validation covers at minimum:

  • enrollment
  • authentication and authorization
  • tenant isolation
  • license/grant issuance
  • signing gateway
  • offline package import/export
  • malformed/archive/path traversal inputs
  • artifact/model upload and verification
  • update execution and rollback
  • replay/rollback
  • transfer/rehost/decommission
  • portal/API privileged actions

High-risk findings must be remediated or explicitly dispositioned before production promotion according to security policy.

docs.title: Support Error Code Catalogue
docs.text: Stable support codes allow customer support, logs and UI to refer to the same failure without exposing stack traces.

docs.title: Naming format
docs.text:
LMS-<DOMAIN>-<HTTP>-<NNN>

Examples:

Code Meaning Operator action LMS-AUTH-401-001 Invalid credentials Verify account; do not disclose which credential failed LMS-DEVICE-409-001 Device already registered to another active identity Start transfer/rehost investigation LMS-DEVICE-409-002 Rehost required after major identity change Submit rehost approval LMS-ENT-409-001 Entitlement pool over-allocation Reduce requested allocation or increase approved entitlement LMS-GRANT-409-001 Stale grant revision Fetch/import newest grant LMS-GRANT-403-002 Feature not entitled Check entitlement/purchase state LMS-OFFLINE-409-001 Offline response does not match request nonce/device Regenerate from fresh request LMS-OFFLINE-409-002 Offline package replay detected Reject; investigate operator/process LMS-CAP-422-001 Workload incompatible with hardware Review capacity recommendations LMS-CAP-409-002 Capacity assessment based on stale inventory Refresh inventory and reassess LMS-REL-422-001 Release incompatible with OS/runtime Select compatible release LMS-REL-409-002 Release blocked by dependency Resolve required runtime/model LMS-UPD-500-001 Install failed; rollback completed Inspect install logs and health-check failure LMS-UPD-500-002 Install failed; rollback also failed Escalate Sev-2/Sev-1 based on scope LMS-SIGN-503-001 Signing service unavailable Retry later; operations alert required

docs.title: Support policy
docs.text: UI shows the stable code and a customer-safe message. Secure logs retain request ID and technical context. Runbooks map critical codes to diagnostic steps.

docs.title: Usage Telemetry Schema
docs.text: High-volume telemetry is logically separate from transactional licensing data. Licensing decisions must not depend on best-effort analytics delivery unless explicitly designed.

docs.title: Planned telemetry families
docs.text:
• camera usage
  • feature usage
  • active hours
  • inference counts
  • trial activity
  • capacity history
  • runtime/application/model versions
  • deployment health

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Operational transactional DB remains PostgreSQL. Telemetry should move to a dedicated analytics/time-series/data-warehouse path when volume justifies it.

docs.title: Privacy open decision
docs.text: Retention, customer opt-in/opt-out, data residency and personally identifiable data policy remain formal open decisions and must be resolved before production telemetry beyond operational necessity.
